facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse says Sudan has one internet exchange point.
Internet Society Pulse says Chad has one IXP managed by ADETIC, with at least nine networks peering there per PeeringDB, almost all visible networks in Chad.

TCD.note: The Trans-Sahara backbone is a proposed cross-border project, not a national backbone.

facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse says Sudan has terrestrial fibre links to Ethiopia, Egypt, South Sudan and Chad and submarine cable links via Port Sudan.
facts.system: Sudan terrestrial links and Port Sudan cable landing

facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse says landlocked Chad reaches international fibre mainly through three cross-border terrestrial fibre links to Sudan and Cameroon.
facts.system: Chad cross-border fibre links to Sudan and Cameroon

TCD.note: Only a rounded count of about 3 million users is given, not a share of the population.

SDN.note: Links to neighbours are named with no shared arrangement or party.

TCD.note: The Trans-Sahara backbone is only described as proposed; no agreement or works stated.
Starlink was still seeking a licence as of September 2023; an application is not a licence.
